name: Claude Haiku 5.5
description: Claude Haiku 5.5 is Anthropic's cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model to date, and the successor to Claude Haiku 4.5. It targets high-volume, cost-sensitive work (summaries, compaction, classification, database queries) and pairs with Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 as a coding subagent; it is especially strong for speed-sensitive tasks like live support and browser use. It is the first Haiku-class model with adjustable effort (low/medium/high/xhigh/max; Claude Platform default medium). It accepts text and image input (including file/PDF) with text output, supports multilingual and vision workloads, tool use, and adaptive thinking. Context window is 1M tokens with 128K max output; knowledge cutoff is June 2026. Claude Platform pricing is tiered by prompt length: prompts up to 100K tokens are $0.10/$0.50 per million input/output (cache read $0.01, 5m cache write $0.125); prompts over 100K are $0.50/$2.50 (cache read $0.05, 5m cache write $0.625). Catalog provider pricing stores the <=100K tier. Capability scores are self-reported from the Claude Haiku 5.5 System Card (Table 8.1.A and §8) and the launch announcement. Available on the Claude API as `claude-haiku-5-5`.

benchmarks.name: AA-Briefcase v1.1
benchmarks.description: AA-Briefcase v1.1 evaluates multi-hour professional office work and reports Elo scores. Kept separate from unversioned AA-Briefcase results.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Announcement + System Card Table 8.1.A / §8.10.3. AA-Briefcase v1.1 Elo (max_score 3000) at max effort. Artificial Analysis independent evaluation. At medium (API default) effort: 1372 Elo.

benchmarks.name: BenchCAD
benchmarks.description: BenchCAD is a benchmark for programmatic CAD reasoning built from 17,900 execution-verified CadQuery programs spanning 106 industrial part families, roughly half anchored to real ISO, DIN, EN, ASME, and IEC specification tables. It decomposes CAD capability into matched tasks; the Vision2Code task requires models to generate CadQuery code from multi-view renders, scored by voxel IoU against the reference geometry.
benchmarks.analysis_method: System Card §8.9.2. BenchCAD Vision2Code 1k subset; voxel IoU 0.670 without tools; adaptive thinking at max effort; averaged over five runs.

benchmarks.name: BenchCAD (with Python tool)
benchmarks.description: BenchCAD variant evaluated with access to a Python tool for programmatic CAD reasoning.
benchmarks.analysis_method: System Card §8.9.2. BenchCAD Vision2Code 1k subset; voxel IoU 0.870 with tools (container with image files and standard libraries, plus an image cropping tool — not a Python CAD tool specifically); adaptive thinking at max effort; averaged over five runs. Kept on the existing with-tools BenchCAD catalog ID (named python-tool); no closer ID exists.

benchmarks.name: Biomedical image analysis
benchmarks.description: Biomedical image analysis: quantitative analyses of biomedical images using domain tools.
benchmarks.analysis_method: System Card §8.13.5. Biomedical image analysis 43.5%; 1 attempt per problem; adaptive thinking at max effort.

benchmarks.name: Chartography

benchmarks.analysis_method: System Card §8.9.1. Chartography with tools 86.2%; adaptive thinking at max effort; container with image file, standard libraries, and image cropping tool.

benchmarks.name: Chartography (no tools)
benchmarks.description: Chartography visual chart recognition evaluated without tools, distinct from tool-assisted results.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Announcement + System Card §8.9.1. Chartography without tools 46.4%; adaptive thinking at max effort.

benchmarks.name: FrontierCode 1.1
benchmarks.description: FrontierCode 1.1 evaluates whether coding-agent changes are mergeable, using unit tests, maintainer-defined rubrics, and verifiers. Runs flagged for unfair internet use receive a zero score.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Announcement + System Card Table 8.1.A / §8.3. FrontierCode v1.1 Main at max effort 46.4% (best Haiku 5.5 effort). Extended 58.4% stored separately.

benchmarks.name: FrontierCode 1.1 (Extended)
benchmarks.description: FrontierCode 1.1 Extended subset: agentic coding tasks graded for mergeable patches, reported separately from the Main subset.
benchmarks.analysis_method: System Card §8.3. FrontierCode v1.1 Extended at max effort 58.4%.

benchmarks.name: FrontierSWE V2
benchmarks.description: FrontierSWE V2 evaluates agents on open-ended technical projects and reports mean@5. Kept separate from FrontierSWE V1 dominance-score results, which are not comparable.
benchmarks.analysis_method: System Card §8.6. FrontierSWE v2; Proximal harness; max effort; 5 trials per task; mean across trials.

benchmarks.name: GDPval-AA 2.1

benchmarks.analysis_method: Announcement + System Card Table 8.1.A / §8.10.2. GDPval-AA v2.1 Elo (max_score 3000) at max effort. Artificial Analysis independent evaluation. At medium (API default) effort: 1277 Elo.

benchmarks.name: Global-MMLU
benchmarks.description: A comprehensive multilingual benchmark covering 42 languages that addresses cultural and linguistic biases in evaluation, with improved translation quality and culturally sensitive question subsets.
benchmarks.analysis_method: System Card §8.12.1. GMMLU average accuracy 87.8% across 42 languages; adaptive thinking at max effort; single trial; no tools.

benchmarks.name: HealthBench
benchmarks.description: An open-source benchmark for measuring performance and safety of large language models in healthcare, consisting of 5,000 multi-turn conversations evaluated by 262 physicians using 48,562 unique rubric criteria across health contexts and behavioral dimensions
benchmarks.analysis_method: System Card §8.11.3. HealthBench length-adjusted 61.6% at max effort. Adaptive thinking at max effort. Raw HealthBench at max was not explicitly reported in the card text.

benchmarks.name: HealthBench Professional
benchmarks.description: HealthBench Professional evaluates model capability and safety for clinician use cases using real clinician-style chats and physician-authored grading rubrics.
benchmarks.analysis_method: System Card Table 8.1.A / §8.11.3. HealthBench Professional length-adjusted score 64.8% at max effort. Raw 71.0% stored separately as healthbench-professional-raw. Adaptive thinking at max effort.

benchmarks.name: HealthBench Professional (raw)
benchmarks.description: HealthBench Professional score before length adjustment. Distinct from the length-adjusted HealthBench Professional catalog metric.
benchmarks.analysis_method: System Card §8.11.3. HealthBench Professional raw (before length adjustment) 71.0% at max effort. Length-adjusted 64.8% is stored as healthbench-professional.

benchmarks.name: Humanity's Last Exam (no tools, text-only)
benchmarks.description: Text-only Humanity's Last Exam variant evaluated without tool use.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Announcement + System Card Table 8.1.A / §8.8.1. HLE without tools; the system card treats HLE as multimodal and does not specify a text-only subset. Adaptive thinking at max effort. Kept on the only existing no-tools HLE catalog ID (historical text-only name); no separate multimodal no-tools ID exists.

benchmarks.name: Humanity's Last Exam (with tools)
benchmarks.description: Full multimodal Humanity's Last Exam evaluated with tool use enabled, distinct from its text-only subset.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Announcement + System Card Table 8.1.A / §8.8.1. HLE with tools (web search, web fetch, programmatic tool calling, code execution); adaptive thinking at max effort.

benchmarks.name: LatchBio SpatialBench Verified

benchmarks.analysis_method: System Card §8.13.1. LatchBio SpatialBench Verified 67.7%; adaptive thinking at max effort; bash/file tools. Biology safeguards off for this capability eval.

benchmarks.name: Medicinal Chemistry (ADME)

benchmarks.analysis_method: System Card §8.13.3. Medicinal Chemistry ADME 58.0% (504 questions); adaptive thinking at max effort.

benchmarks.name: MILU
benchmarks.description: Multi-task Indic Language Understanding (MILU) covers 11 languages—10 Indic languages (Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Tamil, and Telugu) and English—and tests culturally grounded knowledge comprehension.
benchmarks.analysis_method: System Card §8.12.2. MILU average accuracy 87.6% across 11 languages; adaptive thinking at max effort; averaged over 5 trials; no tools.

benchmarks.name: Morphology-to-molecule matching
benchmarks.description: Axiom Bio morphology-to-molecule matching: match multi-channel cell imaging data from a human liver in-vitro assay to shuffled molecule-dose perturbations.
benchmarks.analysis_method: System Card §8.13.2. Axiom Bio morphology-to-molecule matching 25.4%; adaptive thinking at max effort.

benchmarks.name: OfficeQA
benchmarks.description: OfficeQA is a Databricks public benchmark that evaluates end-to-end grounded reasoning over a large corpus of historical U.S. Treasury Bulletin documents. Models must locate relevant tables across the corpus and perform precise numerical reasoning over them.
benchmarks.analysis_method: System Card §8.10.1. OfficeQA full set; max effort; agentic harness with extracted-text documents (mean of five runs).

benchmarks.name: OfficeQA Pro
benchmarks.description: OfficeQA Pro evaluates AI models on professional knowledge-work questions and tasks drawn from real office workflows, including document analysis, spreadsheet reasoning, and information synthesis across business domains.
benchmarks.analysis_method: System Card §8.10.1. OfficeQA Pro (133-question subset); max effort (mean of five runs).

benchmarks.name: OSWorld 2.1 (partial)
benchmarks.description: Partial-credit computer-use score on OSWorld 2.1, as reported in the Claude Sonnet 5.5 release. Separate from OSWorld 2.0 and strict completion scores.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Announcement + System Card Table 8.1.A / §8.9.3. OSWorld 2.1 offline subset (82 of 108 tasks, no internet) partial-credit score 72.4% (Pass@1, 5-run average) at max effort.

benchmarks.name: OSWorld 2.1 (strict)
benchmarks.description: Strict pass rate on OSWorld 2.1: fraction of tasks where every graded checkpoint is satisfied. Separate from the OSWorld 2.1 partial-credit score and from OSWorld 2.0.
benchmarks.analysis_method: System Card §8.9.3. OSWorld 2.1 offline subset strict pass rate 37.1% (every checkpoint satisfied; Pass@1, 5-run average) at max effort.

benchmarks.name: PhysicianBench
benchmarks.description: PhysicianBench is a public benchmark of 100 physician tasks carried out in an electronic health record (EHR), measuring agentic clinical task completion.
benchmarks.analysis_method: System Card §8.11.2. PhysicianBench 100 physician EHR tasks; 43.0% pass rate at max effort (five attempts per task). Safety classifiers enabled.

benchmarks.name: Program Bench
benchmarks.description: Program Bench evaluates code-generation agents by asking them to recreate a program's behavior from only a compiled binary and documentation. It spans 200 tasks from small CLI tools to large systems such as FFmpeg and SQLite, with submissions judged against more than 248,000 fuzz-generated behavioral tests.
benchmarks.analysis_method: System Card §8.7.1. ProgramBench 166 tasks; mini-swe-agent harness; no 6-hour time limit; hidden test pass rate against tests the reference binary passes.

Contains 1,632 high-quality instances carefully annotated from 2,456 candidates by 68 expert annotators, designed to evaluate Large Language Models across diverse software ecosystems beyond Python.

benchmarks.name: SWE-Bench Pro

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench 4.0
benchmarks.description: Terminal-Bench 4.0 evaluates AI agents on real-world work in terminal and command-line containerized environments across 66 tasks, with emphasis on science-adjacent and frontier engineering problems. Relative to earlier Terminal-Bench releases, 4.0 increases timeouts and adaptively raises RAM/CPU on selected tasks to reduce harness and resource confounds.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Announcement + System Card §8.4. Terminal-Bench 4.0 accuracy 39.2% with safeguards enabled (Claude Code --bare, max thinking effort; 10-trial average). No fallback model; safeguard-flagged requests failed (1.8% of trials).

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1
benchmarks.description: Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 is a Stanford-led community benchmark of 70 tasks drawn from scientific research workflows across the life, physical, earth, mathematical, and engineering sciences. Tasks are authored and reviewed by scientists and researchers; scores are typically reported as accuracy with relatively large standard error due to strongly bimodal per-task outcomes.
benchmarks.analysis_method: System Card §8.5. Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1; 20.6% with safeguards enabled (no fallback; 2.3% of trials flagged). Claude Code --bare, max thinking effort.
